name: Use a multimeter
blurb: The diagnostic tool for anything electrical. Four measurements — voltage, continuity, resistance and current — solve most household and automotive electrical mysteries.
gear: A multimeter with a continuity beeper
Batteries and old electronics to practise on
steps: Learn the dial: DC volts, AC volts, resistance, continuity and current, and what the probes plug into for each.
Measure DC voltage on batteries of known state, so you learn what a healthy versus a dead cell reads.
Learn continuity testing: the beeper tells you whether a fuse, switch or wire is intact. This is the single most useful function.
Measure resistance across components with the circuit powered off and the component isolated.
Learn current measurement, which requires breaking the circuit and putting the meter in series — and understand why this blows fuses when done wrong.
Diagnose something real: a dead extension lead, a car battery drain, a suspect fuse.
tips: Never measure resistance or continuity on a live circuit.
Measuring current in parallel across a voltage source is a short circuit. It is the classic way to destroy a meter.
Treat mains voltage with total respect and use a properly rated meter with rated leads.
proof: You diagnose a real electrical fault using the meter to prove where the circuit breaks.
